prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1165; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, waiting for slow-moving traffic ahead when the rear of the vehicle was struck by a pickup operated by Driver 2. Driver 1's vehicle was pushed forward into the stopped car in front, and the impact was consistent with the damage visible to both rear and front bumper areas. A Passenger was seated in the front seat of Driver 1's vehicle and was also present at the scene, and both the Passenger and Driver 2 confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred just as Driver 1 described it, and two independent witnesses who were in nearby vehicles gave matching accounts. Photographs taken at the scene show no prior damage to either vehicle's rear panel, and no earlier collision history was noted. Driver 1 reported neck and back pain and was transported for evaluation, and the reported symptoms fit the speed and force of the impact. Driver 1 was listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
